title: Projects
text:
In progress | Cal Poly Pomona | Master’s thesis project advised by Jayson Smith, Ph.D.
Theoretically, as sea level rises, the zonation patterns of intertidal taxa will shift landward in order for species to stay within their optimal tidal range. The goal of this project, therefore, is to explore long-term shifts in the vertical structure of rocky intertidal communities. I will use a similarity analysis to determine the degree of community structure change among the different target assemblages within a site from a baseline year, likely to be 2004 to each year following through 2024. While temporal vertical shifts in community structure will be compared among each chosen target assemblage, I will focus analyses on my hypothesis that communities in upper assemblages will shift over time and become more similar to the baseline community structure in the lower zone assemblages. For example, I expect that communities in rockweed plots in the mid zone in 2024 will be more similar to the community structure in mussel assemblages measured in 2004, indicating a vertical shift in intertidal taxa.

section: Communications management and International Dark Sky designation
text:
Communications management and International Dark Sky designation
National Park Service | Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve
Management of the Meta Business Suite official social media profiles. Planning and development of interpretive and announcement posts. Production of public announcements for park events. Responding to visitor inquiries through direct messaging and post comments.
Development of core Dark Sky programming for the purpose of International Dark Sky designation. Event planning, leading staff training, and creating official signage and documents.

title: Projects
section: Paleoclimatology & paleoceanography: Seawater temperature reconstruction using marine fossils
text:
Paleoclimatology & paleoceanography: Seawater temperature reconstruction using marine fossils
UCLA | Tripati Lab
Clumped-isotope analysis of benthic foraminifera fossils (10Ma - recent) from the Southern Ocean. Reconstruction of deep seawater temperature through time, including the warm late Miocene and Pliocene - Pleistocene transition.

title: Welcome!
text: Hi! My name is Gwyneth Stolo and I am a current graduate student and park ranger. My interests include community ecology, global change ecology, palentology, cave and karst geology, and science interpretation.
